flags.observation: "Goldberg's shoulder smashed into the ring-post" names a real wrestler inside an otherwise fictional animal cast, a sudden drop into real-world specificity.
"Stay Fluffy, Folks!" follows the quiet "Close the lid gently." with an upbeat sign-off, a tone swing right at the close.
"And there is a canvas bag in the corner nobody opens." breaks the animal-teacher pattern built across prior beats, bringing in an inanimate object rather than an animal body.
"And one big eye on the shelf." again drops the animal cast for an object, forming with beat 13 a mixed roster of teachers.
"That one is mine. The others are on loan." states the performer's whole situation in two short sentences.
"the opossum by the crayons, staggering from a tiny tap" renders the wrestling sell technique as a literal animal behavior, a concrete image for an abstract term.

fractalCards.observation: Each card is voiced through an animal body performing its trait, but the card text itself describes the technique in third person rather than the animal making a first-person claim about itself.

individuality.observation: Each wrestling concept rides a specific animal body, "The kangaroo next to him swears by this one" for the thigh slap, "The donkey answers with a thud" for the stomp, a concrete device rather than a generic trope list.

outro.observation: "Close the lid gently." lands as tender, but the following "Stay Fluffy, Folks!" turns the close into an upbeat sign-off, a tone jump right after the quiet final image.

performer.observation: The voice carries resignation and dry humor: "I'm plastic. Performing is the whole job." and "That one is mine. The others are on loan." give it a steady, specific personality.

resident.observation: The figure speaks to "Whoever holds the box." from inside its own toy-box world, performing whether "nobody is" there or someone is, not reciting facts outward to an audience.

standalone.observation: Every named item gets a plain-language gloss right where it lands, as with "high-flying moves, because audiences cheer for that," so the jargon rarely leans on outside knowledge.

storyBetweenCards.observation: The cards move from character types through selling tricks and production fakery to a turn, "Then one night a head really cracks.", then to the finisher and close, a real arc, not a flat list.

transferable.observation: The wrestling vocabulary, the animal cast, and the toy-box frame are bound together closely enough that none of it reads as a label sitting on top of a different subject.

lyrics:
[Spoken Word]

Lid's open. A kid is back, or you are, or nobody is and the box just creaked. I perform anyway. I'm plastic. Performing is the whole job.

Big Bad Brain Wrestling, it says on the lid. One body, four heads, a cardboard ring. Every head is somebody else, and every one of them swears the fight is real.

Click. Golden head. The Babyface: high-flying moves, because audiences cheer for that. A slave to approval.

Click. Sneer head. The Heel: brutal, sneaky moves. If they aren't booing, you aren't doing your job.

Click. Sunglasses. The Tweener: the audience decides to cheer for you on their own. You don't ask for it.

And the head that came in the package. The Jobber: isolated and picked apart. You exist to make the other guy look good.

That one is mine. The others are on loan.

My teacher is the opossum by the crayons, staggering from a tiny tap: The Master Seller: maintain the illusion of peril. Limp to the ring. Make them believe.

The kangaroo next to him swears by this one: The Thigh Slap: slapping the thigh when kicking. A loud sound suggests impact. An audio lie.

The donkey answers with a thud: The Stomp Punch: stomping on the mat when punching. Kinetic misdirection.

The chicken overdoes it, every time. The Oversell Clown: reacting to an attack far beyond reality. A mockery of the sport.

The axolotl keeps her mask on, even in the dark. The Sacred Mask: kayfabe sacred to their identity. The biggest identifier. Never remove it.

And there is a canvas bag in the corner nobody opens. The Snake Bag: the bag has a live snake. Terrify them before the match starts.

Who decides how it ends? Look up. Whoever holds the box.

Or the spider in the suit, pulling strings: The Booker: the ending is pre-planned. You are just a puppet.

The cricket calls the next move into my ear. The Spot Caller: calling moves in the ring. A basic outline, filled in with sweat.

And one big eye on the shelf. The Hard Cam: if the camera didn't see it, it didn't happen.

Most nights it's this one. The Empty Arena: taped in empty arenas, pausing for a pop that never comes. Surreal.

So the chameleons on the wall pretend to be a crowd. The Green Screen Crowd: a failed attempt to hide the emptiness. Audio sweetening on a lie.

Then one night a head really cracks. The Real Injury: Goldberg's shoulder smashed into the ring-post. The crowd goes nuts: it's real.

The cop in the corner is writing me up for telling you this. The Kayfabe Police: protecting the business. Keep the secrets secret, or get fired.

[Bell]

Here it comes. The Finisher: the Leg Drop. The most important moment. If this hits, go home.

It hits. And the zebra still kicks out, The False Finish: the art of the near-fall, kicking out at two point nine nine, crowd vertical.

So I lie down the way the phoenix does. The Retirement Match: leaning on the fourth wall. Rising, and falling. See you next season.

One line on the package is still true. When defeated, you may choose who defeats you. That is your only control.

So whoever opened the lid: it's you. You knew the ending and stayed for the near-fall anyway.

Out there they swear it's real. In here it says plastic on the label, and I still give you everything. Close the lid gently. All my heads are in here.

Stay Fluffy, Folks!

styleA: Glam rock stomp at 118 BPM: pounding floor toms and handclaps on two and four, fuzzed power chords, honky-tonk piano, booming bass, a toy piano doubling the riff, a short gang shout on the big hits. One weathered male tenor speak-singing close to the mic, tired and warm, cracking upward on the peaks. Roomy drums, saturated tape, dry intimate vocal on top.
styleB: Boom-bap hip-hop at 100 BPM: dusty swung drums, a looped vinyl brass sample, upright bass, scratched stabs, plastic clicks as percussion, sparse Rhodes chords. One gravelly male voice, conversational and late on the beat, half laughing at himself. Crisp vocal, long drop-outs before the last lines.
